title: Blaschka source corpus ingest priority
principle: Prioritize sources that can be ingested now or retrieved by a precise archival unit. Repository discovery alone has lower value than document-level or corpus-level access.

priorities.target: Harvard HOLLIS ecb00006 digital archive — Blaschka studio correspondence + Ware correspondence
priorities.access: open digital surrogates linked from archival finding aid
priorities.action: Download the finding-aid CSV; create a component-level hierarchy; harvest digital-surrogate links for Series I correspondence; preserve archival hierarchy, call number, date and repository provenance before text/image extraction.
priorities.reason: HOLLIS currently reports 2,749 archival components and 897 digital-content components and states that most Series I correspondence is digitised.
priorities.guard: 897 is HOLLIS's digital-content component metric, not a count of digitised letters or pages.

priorities.target: BHL Rudolf Blaschka letters to Walter Deane, 1895–1927
priorities.access: open digital, with BHL OCR/text and multiple Plazi/Zenodo part-level PDF mirrors
priorities.action: Download OCR/text and page metadata; preserve display-label and structured-date fields separately; record BHL part IDs and Zenodo DOIs where available; create one record per dated correspondence part/page.
priorities.reason: Large direct primary corpus available immediately with no archive visit and persistent part-level surrogates for multiple letters.

priorities.access: open/downloadable digital primary sources identified by Corning Museum of Glass
priorities.action: Ingest page-by-page customer/order/account entries and align with local OCR, dealer registers and current-holder census without collapsing historical purchaser into present repository.
priorities.reason: Transaction backbone for original customers, sales and dealer shares.

priorities.action: Cross-walk Harvard, Deane, business books, packing/shipping and live-animal supply records while preserving drafts/copies/enclosures as distinct witnesses.

priorities.target: R. T. Smith, Weymouth — cross-project living-specimen and microscopy corpus
priorities.access: local Rakow OCR + local Hardwicke's Science-Gossip corpus + published archival locators
priorities.action: Build one chronology from the five exact microscopy notices (1873–1876), 1882/1886 workshop drafts, species requests, 15-Mark order, forwarding language, weather, transit duration, aquarium recovery/failure and alternative Devon supplier search; image-verify before diplomatic quotation.
priorities.reason: Immediate person/address bridge between two local corpora and a direct upstream living-reference route.
priorities.guard: Do not merge the Hughes/Lloyd OCR reading 'E. J. Smith, 25 St. Alban's Row' with R. T. Smith until the printed page is checked.

priorities.target: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn, Naples — 4 February 1877 Leopold Blaschka species-list letter + March/November 1877 archive documents
priorities.access: precise archive retrieval; institutional archive and published archival references identified
priorities.action: Obtain image and shelfmark for the reported 4 February 1877 letter requesting 41 preserved marine animals; retrieve the March and November 1877 Dohrn documents; cross-walk request, fulfilment, prices, species, preservation and shipment.
priorities.reason: This is the strongest known upstream preserved-reference transaction: exact date, quantity, purpose and named institutional supplier, with a rich ASZN administrative/scientific archive behind it.
priorities.guard: The 41-item list is reported by a scholar who examined the Naples archive; do not enter species-level transcription until the archival document is obtained.

priorities.target: Trieste reciprocal circuit — live-animal shipments 1878–1884+ and Vienna/Graz model orders
priorities.access: local Rudolf primary OCR + University of Vienna institutional reconstruction + Austrian State Archives Signatur 2A
priorities.action: Cross-walk Rudolf's direct Trieste statement with Rakow drafts, Vienna order chronology and OeStA Zoologische Station Triest 1873–1903; target 1878 live shipments, 1880 rupture, 1884 restored exchange, orders of 38 and 77, and February 1887 order of 21.
priorities.reason: Best case where inward biological supply and outward model distribution form one reciprocal institutional circuit. It directly tests how routing, temperature, packing and survival changed epistemic inputs before manufacture.

priorities.target: Reference-material ecology — Müller/Gosse illustrations + Naples preserved animals + Trieste/Smith living animals + workshop drawings
priorities.access: open museum/archive sources + local primary corpus
priorities.action: Build model/species-level crosswalks only where a drawing, catalogue number, archival statement or object identification explicitly connects reference medium to model. Code published image, preserved body, living observation and workshop drawing separately.
priorities.reason: Converts 'scientific accuracy' from a generic claim into a source-history problem with distinct affordances and failure modes.

priorities.target: University of Rochester A.W23 and D.231 Ward archives
priorities.action: Request or inspect Blaschka-specific customer correspondence, invoices, catalogue/order records, packing/shipping and account rows.
priorities.reason: Only concentrated dealer-side personal + corporate archive in the three principal distribution routes.

priorities.target: Cornell Comstock papers Box 2 Folder 7 and reported 1882 Andrew D. White letter
priorities.action: Read Ward letters of 3, 8 and 23 October 1885; locate the reported 16 October 1882 Ward-to-White letter; test whether Cornell acquisition occurred in multiple Ward-mediated layers.
priorities.reason: Precise 1885 Ward folder plus testable claim for an earlier 1882 procurement layer.

priorities.target: UCD Archives IE UCDA RCSI accounts 1883–1885 and equipment/supplies order books 1867–1916
priorities.action: Search exact 13 June 1885 transaction and 495/619-Mark totals; identify any intermediary/commission notation.
priorities.reason: May close the unexplained 124-Mark commission layer.

priorities.target: Charles Francis Adams Diary, Illinois collection 782
priorities.action: Read January–May 1885 entries around Ward shipment arrival; code wharf, package, museum handoff, unpacking and payment references.
priorities.reason: Personal archive of a named carrier/preparator/payment intermediary in the Auckland transaction.

priorities.target: MNCN/Simurg Robert F. Damon catalogues and dispatch note, 1885–1906
priorities.action: Transcribe catalogue headings, list structure, prices if present, customer/dispatch notation and language.
priorities.reason: Same-period Damon business paperwork supplies a control vocabulary for British/Irish transactions.

priorities.target: Smithsonian SIA RU007095 Box 1 specimen lists, 1861–1865
priorities.action: Isolate Damon lists and financial entries and compare with Talling/Vaux inside the same customer archive.
priorities.reason: Controlled pre-agency comparator for dealer list, purchase and exchange practices.

priorities.target: Corning premade component stock / matchbox corpus
priorities.action: Inventory labelled matchboxes/component types and cross-walk with catalogue numbers, order books, schematic drawings and finished models where possible.
priorities.reason: Tests the chronology between order receipt and manufacture: some production occurred before the order and later assembly/finishing could be order-triggered.

priorities.target: Frič–Antipa letters nos. 168–172 and associated inventory/registers
priorities.action: Use as coding template for dealer → receiving inventory → surviving object crosswalk.
priorities.reason: Excellent longitudinal comparator but postdates Blaschka marine-model production.

priorities.target: BayHStA ZSS 113/124/127 and related dealer acquisition files
priorities.action: Compare Frič, Damon, Ward and adjacent dealers under one museum administrative system.
priorities.reason: Best controlled receiving-side comparison for ordinary natural-history dealership.

priorities.target: Carrier/customs archives: Lloyd Triestino, NDL, NARA RG36
priorities.action: Search only against already known case marks, shipment dates, consignee/forwarder names and routes.
priorities.reason: High interpretive value but lower expected hit rate than direct correspondence/account sources.
